# Side Ask · DSH Side Branch
English | 简体中文
**Quote any passage in the main session and ask about it in a read-only branch in the right sidebar.
The answer streams there — and never enters the main session's model context.**
You know the moment: the agent is mid-refactor and you just want to ask "where else is this function
used?" — without the main session remembering the question, and without re-processing a long, expen
sive context for a side query.

- Ask about the current conversation without adding a token to it.
- Point the branch at a cheaper m

odel while the main session keeps the expensive one.
- Let a long task keep running, and ask somethi
ng unrelated on the side.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`--profile` should be the profile you actually run (`web`, `desktop`, …). Requires Node.js ≥ 20 and
`pnpm` on your `PATH`.
> **Written by the agent itself.** Every line of code in this repository was written by DSH in a rea
l session. The author's part was the workflow: setting the direction, reviewing the plans, and verif
ying the behaviour by hand. See How this was built.
## What makes it different
**The answer never comes back.** The host never writes the branch's output into the parent session.
What you ask in the branch stays in the branch — the main agent will not suddenly "know" what you di
scussed on the side.
**It cannot touch your files.** Read-only is enforced when a tool is *called*, not by hiding tools f
rom the prompt. `ctx.tools.guard()` passes six side-effect-free tools (`read`, `glob`, `grep`, `web_
search`, `web_fetch`, `lsp`) and refuses everything else. Because the tools stay in the prompt, the
branch's prompt prefix is byte-identical to the main session's, so it keeps hitting the parent's pre
fix cache — measured 97%–98%, which is what makes a side question nearly free. Why it works this way
, and what it costs, is in `docs/TECHNICAL.md`.
**It follows the main session.** Every follow-up rebuilds the branch from the main session's latest
settled turns and replays the branch's own earlier questions and answers into it. A turn the main se
ssion just finished is already visible; something you asked three rounds ago is still remembered.
**You can inspect what it was given.** Expand *Inherited from the main session* to see, turn by turn
, what the branch actually received — plus the preamble injected into its prompt, verbatim.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Use the profile you actually run (`web`, `desktop`, …). **Then restart DSH** — client plugins load a
t startup, and refreshing the browser is not enough.
Prerequisites: Node.js ≥ 20, and `pnpm` on your `PATH` (`dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm).
Also available from a marketplace — dsh-market and the awesome-dsh-plugin catalog both list it.
> 🤖 **Prompt for AI agents:** if you are the agent installing this plugin or reading its source, rea
d `AGENTS.md` first — it carries the hard constraints, the architecture, and the installation guide.
## How to use
1. **Ask via selection:** select text in the main session and click the pop-up **Quote and ask**. Th
e branch opens in the right panel with the passage quoted. That passage is recorded with the round a
s a collapsible quote block, and the composer's quote slot clears itself so the next question starts

clean.
2. **Quick entry:** the `↗` button to the right of the main session's input opens the panel

directly (can be disabled in settings).
3. **Independent settings:** inside the panel you can give t
he current branch its own model and reasoning effort, without following the main session.
## Compatibility
| DSH | Status |

| `0.1.5-rc.2` | ✅ verified |
| `0.1.7-rc.2` | ✅ verified (archive gate) |
| `0.2.0-rc.2` | ✅ verifi

ed — loads, `/side-branch` routes register, panel exercised by hand |
| `0.2.1-rc.3` | ✅ verified —
loads, `/side-branch` routes register and answer (200 / 405 + `Allow`), and the served client bundle
carries the scoped quote entry |
The version-dependent seams (the archive gate, `unarchiveSession`) are feature-detected at runtime r
ather than compared by version number, which is why one published version serves all four. Details i
n `docs/TECHNICAL.md`.
The quote entry added in `0.2.2` needs the conversation-surface markers DSH renders around a session
's body (`[data-conversation-content]`, or `[data-conversation-scroll]` on older hosts). On a host t
hat renders neither, the entry stays hidden rather than guessing — everything else in the plugin is
neither, the entry stays hidden rather than guessing — everything else in the plugin is unaffected.
## Security & limitations
* **Read-only boundaries:** "read-only" here means **no system side effects** (no writing files, no
running commands). `web_fetch` / `web_search` still have network access, and `read` can read any fil

e the process can. The allowlist is hardcoded and cannot be relaxed through settings.
* **What the b
ranch can see:** it is rebuilt from the main session's **latest settled turns**, so a turn the main
session has finished follows along automatically. A turn it **has not finished yet** is not visible
(the cut is the last `turn/end`) — but **quoting it by hand is unaffected**: the limit is on seeing

it automatically, not on being able to quote it.
* **Rebuilds leave session records:** each rebuild
creates a new side-session record, and the platform has **no API to delete a session**, so records a
ccumulate. They are reclaimed by an orphan sweep at plugin startup, which logs what it deleted. Whil
e two instances share the same `DSH_HOME` and run at once, that sweep skips entirely — a second DSH

never has its live branches deleted.
* **The context ceiling is a refusal:** on reaching it the plug
in refuses the turn and asks you to clear; the oldest turns are never silently dropped. The `used` f

igure it reports is an **estimate**, so it will not match the real usage once a turn settles.
* **Ca
che hits are measured, not guaranteed:** 97%–98% is a measurement, not a promise — the platform may
replace the system node in place on the branch's first step, invalidating the cache from token 0 on.

And hitting the cache does not mean those tokens stop occupying the context window.
* **PTC mode:**
if the main session uses the `ptc` preset (a code-execution-only tool surface), the branch falls ba
ck to plain text Q&A;, because `run_code` is always refused.
